samples.summary: `htmlLabels: false` does not close the layout-window beacon class: mermaid's shape metadata (`A@{ img: "https://attacker/beacon" }`, icon shapes) emits an SVG `<image href>` into the live layout host regardless of label mode
samples.evidence: The fix's whole claim (module note lines 51-63, docs `notes.md`) is that with `htmlLabels: false` "there is no label subtree to lay out", so nothing fetches during measurement. Mermaid 11 node metadata carries an image shape independent of label rendering — `flowchart LR\n  A@{ img: "https://attacker.example/beacon.png" }` — which the renderer materializes as an SVG `<image href=…>` inside the `d<id>` host div appended to `document.body` (mermaid.ts:518-520 documents that host). The browser fetches that href the moment it is parsed, i.e. strictly before `sanitizeSvg()` runs, so the note author still gets every reader's IP, UA and read time. `FORBID_TAGS: ['img','image', …]` (mermaid.ts:281) removes it only from what persists — the exact reasoning error the change's own lessons doc identifies. Same shape of residual carrier for `icon:` shapes if an icon pack is ever registered. I could not confirm against the installed engine (no `node_modules/mermaid` in the tree, so I could not grep `imageSquare`/shape handling), hence medium confidence; nothing in the diff or the suite tests a non-label fetch carrier.

samples.summary: Only the ROOT `htmlLabels` is set; label paths that read the per-diagram key (`flowchart.htmlLabels`, default true) and the diagram types the change itself admits emit `foreignObject` unconditionally keep parsing note-derived HTML into the live document
samples.evidence: mermaid.initialize() (mermaid.ts:473-479) sets root `htmlLabels: false` only, and the comment at mermaid.ts:470-472 asserts the engine resolves labels through `config.htmlLabels ?? config.flowchart?.htmlLabels ?? true`. Not every label path goes through that chain: mermaid reads `evaluate(getConfig().flowchart.htmlLabels)` directly in its edge-label/legacy label helpers, and `flowchart.htmlLabels` defaults to true — so `A -- "" --> B` (edge label rather than node label) would still be measured as a `` HTML subtree in the live document, refiring the exact issue #721 beacon. Mermaid's own strict-mode `sanitizeText` uses DOMPurify's DEFAULT allowlist (it only adds `FORBID_TAGS: ['style']`), which permits `` — which is why the original bug existed at all. The change also documents (PURIFY_CONFIG comment mermaid.ts:259-264, notes.md, lessons doc) that venn text nodes, architecture icons, kanban and sequence emit `foreignObject` "with no `htmlLabels` guard"; note text reaching those subtrees is the same pre-fetch window, and the lessons doc justifies leaving them with "`img`/`image` are already forbidden" — i.e. layer 3, which the same document correctly says is not a fetch boundary. Hardening: also pin `flowchart/class/state/er/…: { htmlLabels: false }` (a nested key `secure` cannot pin) or take `securityLevel: 'sandbox'` / an `img-src` CSP. Medium confidence: the installed mermaid is not present in the tree, so I could not grep `edges.js`/`createLabel.js` to confirm which key each path reads.

samples.summary: The new fixpoint loop makes carrier stripping quadratic in an unbounded, attacker-controlled fence body — a stored main-thread DoS on every reader; the `maxTextSize` bound the comment leans on is enforced only inside `mermaid.render()`, i.e. after the strip
samples.evidence:
`stripConfigDirectives()` now loops (mermaid.ts:251-255). Each iteration removes at most ONE front-matter block (`FRONTMATTER_RE` is non-global and `^`-anchored) but pays a full global `DIRECTIVE_RE` scan plus two whole-string allocations, so a fence of k stacked `---
x
---
` blocks costs O(k·N) ≈ O(N²/8). The comment's own numbers confirm the scaling: 1.5 ms at 10 kB, 29 ms at 50 kB (≈20x for 5x input). It is called at mermaid.ts:504 on the raw fence body — mermaid's `maxTextSize` guard runs inside `mermaid.render()`, after the strip, so the 50 kB figure is not a bound on this input. I found no note/fence length cap anywhere in packages/notes (grepped for `maxTextSize`, `MAX_`, `slice(0,`, `content.length`) and `preview.ts:198` renders whatever the note contains. A collaborator or editor-role share-link visitor stores one ~2-5 MB fence of stacked front-matter blocks and every reader's tab freezes for minutes on open (the pass is synchronous on the main thread); several such fences in one note add up, and each theme switch re-keys the cache and re-pays it. Mitigation: cap the input length (or the iteration count) before looping, or make the front-matter pattern remove all leading blocks in one anchored pass.

samples.summary: `SECURE_KEYS` — the layer-1 pin the change now relies on for `htmlLabels` — omits `dompurifyConfig`, the one config key that relaxes mermaid's own label sanitizer, turning a missed carrier from a beacon into script execution
samples.evidence: SECURE_KEYS (mermaid.ts:178-195) replaces mermaid's default `secure` list and enumerates theming/label keys, but not `dompurifyConfig`. Mermaid's strict-mode `sanitizeText` passes `config.dompurifyConfig` straight to DOMPurify, so a config carrier that layer 2 misses could deliver `{"dompurifyConfig":{"ADD_TAGS":["script"],"ADD_ATTR":["onerror"]}}` and get script/event-handler markup into any surviving HTML label subtree — which the engine parses into `document.body` during measurement (mermaid.ts:45-49), i.e. it executes before `sanitizeSvg()` exists. `legacyMathML`/`forceLegacyMathML` are similarly unpinned and switch KaTeX label output from MathML to HTML. The module's own stated model (mermaid.ts:32-35, notes.md 'a carrier the strip under-recognizes still delivers a nested override') is that layer 1's pin must hold when layer 2 misses, so this is a real gap in the defense the change strengthens. Related: `secure` pins top-level keys only, so the nested `flowchart.htmlLabels` the previous finding relies on cannot be pinned here at all — the diff's claim that the key is 'pinned in SECURE_KEYS … so a note cannot turn it back on' holds only for the root spelling.
searchedFor: grep for dompurifyConfig across packages (no hits)

samples.summary: The test titled 'sets an htmlLabels key the real engine actually honors' proves only that the config round-trips, not that any label path honors it — the security claim of the change has no test behind it
samples.evidence: preview.test.ts:639-645 calls real `mermaid.initialize({… htmlLabels:false})` and asserts `mermaid.mermaidAPI.getConfig().htmlLabels === false`. `getConfig()` returns the merged site config, so this passes for ANY key mermaid's config merge accepts, honored or not — a renderer that reads `flowchart.htmlLabels` (default true) would leave this green while the beacon is wide open, which is precisely the regression the comment claims to catch. It also does not pass `secure: SECURE_KEYS`, so it does not exercise the production initialize shape, and it mutates the process-global engine config for later cases. Every other new case uses a stub engine, so nothing in the suite asserts the absence of a network fetch or of a `<foreignObject>`/`<image>` in the layout host. Suggest an assertion on the engine's actual output instead (e.g. render a label payload and assert no `foreignObject`/`image` element and no fetch attempt) or, if jsdom cannot render, state plainly in the test name that only config retention is covered.
searchedFor: grep for jsdom render / fetch spies in preview.test.ts

verdict.reason: The finding is present as described and I could not refute it on any named ground. mermaid.ts:41-63 and docs/design/notes/notes.md:503-510 both concede that mermaid lays the diagram out in a live `d<id>` host div appended to document.body before sanitizeSvg() runs (confirmed in production code by the cleanup at mermaid.ts:513-521), so DOMPurify's FORBID_TAGS ['img','image',...] (mermaid.ts:281) and ALLOWED_URI_REGEXP (mermaid.ts:296) govern only what persists, not what is fetched. The only claimed mitigation is `htmlLabels: false` (mermaid.ts:473-479), which suppresses only HTML *label* subtrees; it says nothing about mermaid 11 node metadata (`A@{ img: "…" }`) that renders an SVG <image href> / preloads the URL independently of label mode. stripConfigDirectives() (mermaid.ts:249-256, patterns 220-222) strips only `%%{…}%%` directives and leading front matter, so `@{ img: … }` metadata reaches mermaid.render() untouched (mermaid.ts:504) — no upstream guard exists. There is also no app CSP (grep for Content-Security-Policy/img-src matched only vendored .trusted/node_modules; notes.md:523-524 states the repo has no CSP), so nothing ambient blocks the request. The test suite only asserts the htmlLabels flag is passed and honored (preview.test.ts:616-646) and exercises a stub engine elsewhere, so no non-label fetch carrier is covered. Impact is squarely in the security lane: a note author harvests every reader's IP, User-Agent and read time from another user's session — the exact disclosure class this change claims to close. `not-present` fails (code is as described), `already-guarded` fails (no guard found), `out-of-scope` fails (sensitive data exposure via note-controlled outbound fetch). I could not inspect the installed engine (no node_modules/mermaid in the tree), and that residual uncertainty argues for keeping the finding, not dropping it.

verdict.reason: The absence is real and I could not find any counterexample. SECURE_KEYS (mermaid.ts:178-195) enumerates 14 keys and explicitly replaces mermaid's default `secure` list (comment at :179); `dompurifyConfig`, `legacyMathML` and `forceLegacyMathML` are absent. mermaid.ts:473-479 is the sole `mermaid.initialize()` call in product code, so this is the only pin that exists, and a repo-wide grep for `dompurifyConfig|legacyMathML|forceLegacyMathML` returns zero hits — the key is not pinned, filtered, or mentioned anywhere else. No compensating control blunts the escalation: the only CSP in the tree is `frame-ancestors 'none'` on an unrelated CLI-login page (cli-login-confirm.middleware.ts:166), and notes.md:523 states the repo has no CSP. The pre-sanitize execution window is documented in-repo (mermaid.ts:44-49: the engine lays out in document.body before sanitizeSvg() runs; "Layer 3 governs what persists; it is not a fetch boundary"), and surviving HTML label subtrees exist even with htmlLabels:false because PURIFY_CONFIG deliberately keeps the HTML profile and `foreignobject` for venn/architecture/kanban/sequence labels (mermaid.ts:259-277). The module's own model (mermaid.ts:32-35, notes.md:480-482) is that top-level `secure` pinning is the backstop for a carrier the strip under-recognizes, and dompurifyConfig is exactly that class of top-level key — the one that relaxes mermaid's own sanitizeText DOMPurify call. The only candidate mitigation is layer 2 (stripConfigDirectives, mermaid.ts:249-256), which cannot refute a defense-in-depth gap in the layer built to survive its failure; I also could not diff its verbatim patterns against upstream because mermaid is not installed in this tree. Caveat: exploitation today requires a layer-2 carrier miss I could not demonstrate, but severity reflects impact-if-real, not certainty.
